title: Compass and Ledger
premise: In the Baltic port city of Vessengard, 1919, Ulyana Eriksen works as a compositor in her late father's print shop, convinced that revolutions are things that happen to capitals and grandees, not to girls who set type. When a wounded courier named Anton arrives bearing letters in her father's unmistakable hand — three years after his reported death at the front — she learns he survived, deserted, and has been documenting war crimes by the very general now negotiating the armistice. As factions close in on the shop and its evidence, Ulyana must choose between fleeing with Anton and staying to print the truth before the victors' historians can bury it. The book ends with the pamphlet distributed through the armistice crowds, her father's fate revealed but unresolved, and Ulyana claiming her place as keeper of the record rather than an invisible bystander.
about_author: Beatrix Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime printing presses and censored newspapers across Northern Europe. She writes historical fiction about the people whose hands actually made history — typesetters, couriers, and clerks.

chapters.title: The Smell of Ink
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A day in the Eriksen print shop: setting type for shipping manifests, banter with apprentice Milo, quiet grief for her father declared dead two years past. Establishes her belief that history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: comfortable numbness about to crack.

chapters.title: Manifests and Margins
chapters.summary: Ulyana notices odd insertions in a government print order — pages that don't match the ledger. Her POV; suspicion planted. She says nothing, telling herself it isn't her business. Beat: the first small cost of looking away.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Loading Door
chapters.summary: Anton arrives at night, feverish, carrying a satchel he refuses to open. Ulyana's POV. She hides him from a patrol out of instinct rather than conviction. Beat: fear mixed with a strange recognition of purpose.

chapters.title: Handwriting Like a Face
chapters.summary: Anton produces letters written by Ulyana's father — alive, or recently so. Her POV; shock, denial, fury at being lied to. Milo senses something is wrong. Beat: grief reopens as hope, which is crueler.

chapters.title: What the Courier Carried
chapters.summary: Anton explains: her father survived, deserted, and gathered testimony of atrocities under General Halvard's command. Ulyana's POV, interleaved with Anton's account. Beat: the world tilts; invisibility was always an illusion.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Ulyana searches her father's old business ledgers and finds coded entries matching Anton's documents. Dual focus on her discovery and her mother's fragile health upstairs. Beat: the past was speaking all along.

chapters.title: Milo Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. He notices the locked back room and Anton's bandages; loyalty wars with self-preservation. He chooses to help, quietly. Beat: belonging tested and affirmed.

chapters.title: The Compositor's Art
chapters.summary: Ulyana teaches Anton how type is set while they plan a pamphlet. Tender, technical chapter; intimacy grows without being named. Beat: two fugitives building something together.

chapters.title: Inspector Brandt Calls
chapters.summary: A state inspector visits the shop on a routine censorship sweep. Ulyana's POV; a cat-and-mouse conversation over tea where every sentence has two meanings. Beat: terror managed with etiquette.

chapters.title: Letters to a Ghost
chapters.summary: Ulyana reads her father's full letters alone at night. Flashbacks to childhood in the shop. Beat: anger at him curdling into understanding of what survival costs.

chapters.title: The Printers' Guild
chapters.summary: Anton seeks allies among guild masters; most refuse, one old master, Signe Holm, agrees secretly. Anton's POV. Beat: hope that must be rationed.

chapters.title: Paper Is Rationed
chapters.summary: The practical problem: no legal paper stock for a clandestine run. Ulyana schemes to divert misprinted manifest stock. Milo's POV during the theft. Beat: petty crime as moral clarity.

chapters.title: Halvard Comes to Town
chapters.summary: General Halvard arrives for armistice preparations; parades, posters, his face everywhere. Ulyana watches from the crowd, sickened. Beat: power as spectacle, corruption as pageantry.

chapters.title: Signe's Cellar Press
chapters.summary: Rehearsal run on Signe's hidden press; mechanical failures, near-discovery by a neighbor. Ensemble scene. Beat: camaraderie forged in grease and panic.

chapters.title: What Anton Did
chapters.summary: Anton confesses his own complicity as a soldier who followed orders before defecting. Ulyana must decide if a guilty man can carry truth. Beat: the price of survival, paid in shame.

chapters.title: Brandt Returns
chapters.summary: Inspector Brandt, sharper now, questions the missing paper stock. Ulyana lies fluently and hates how good she's become. Beat: corruption touches her own hands.

chapters.title: Mother Knows
chapters.summary: Ulyana's mother reveals she has known about the letters for weeks and gives her blessing — and her wedding silver to sell for supplies. Beat: generational courage; belonging deepens.

chapters.title: The First Proof
chapters.summary: First proof sheet pulled: her father's testimony in readable form. Ulyana reads aloud to the group. Beat: awe — words becoming weapons.

chapters.title: A Betrayal Overheard
chapters.summary: Milo's cousin, drunk, lets slip that something moves through the shop. Milo's POV; he confronts and half-silences him, too late. Beat: dread tightening.

chapters.title: The Raid Next Door
chapters.summary: Soldiers raid the neighboring bindery; the group watches from the cellar as their neighbor is dragged out. Ulyana's POV. Beat: the cost of the cause made flesh.

chapters.title: Signe Pays
chapters.summary: Signe Holm is arrested; her press seized. Anton blames himself; Ulyana refuses to stop. Argument over whether truth is worth lives. Beat: the theme sharpened into conflict.

chapters.title: Armistice Terms Leak
chapters.summary: Through printed proofs they learn the armistice will be signed within ten days — and Halvard's crimes will be amnestied in the fine print. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Planning montage: distribution routes via fish carts and choir lofts, Milo forging passes. Tense, procedural. Beat: ordinary people becoming extraordinary.

chapters.title: Brandt's Offer
chapters.summary: Brandt privately offers Ulyana immunity to hand over Anton, revealing he knows more than he should — perhaps sympathizes. Beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: The Letter That Isn't His
chapters.summary: Ulyana discovers one letter is forged — planted to lure them. Paranoia fractures trust; Anton falls under suspicion. Beat: doubt as the enemy's best weapon.

chapters.title: Eight Days
chapters.summary: Ulyana verifies authenticity using her father's private kerning habits — only he would space an 'f' that way. Trust restored, deeper than before. Beat: expertise as love.

chapters.title: Where Father Is
chapters.summary: Anton admits her father is alive but imprisoned in the fortress pending transfer — the amnesty would erase him entirely. Beat: stakes become personal and immediate.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Plan splits: print run continues while Anton scouts the fortress. Ulyana runs the press alone for the first time. Beat: inheritance claimed.

chapters.title: The Break-In
chapters.summary: Soldiers search the shop; Ulyana hides galleys inside a coffin ordered for a funeral job. Milo's POV. Beat: gallows humor under mortal fear.

chapters.title: Four Days
chapters.summary: Anton captured scouting the fortress. Ulyana receives a note offering both men for the plates. Beat: despair, then resolve — she will not trade the truth.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Ulyana visits Brandt with a counter-offer: the pamphlet's distribution already beyond recall; his name appears in it as a man who looked away. Beat: power inverted through print.

chapters.title: Two Days
chapters.summary: Night print run — 3,000 copies. Physical, exhausting, joyful. Milo injured but presses on. Beat: labor as devotion.

chapters.title: One Day
chapters.summary: Distribution begins; bundles vanish into the city like water into sand. First copies read aloud in taverns. Beat: exhilaration and terror entwined.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: Armistice signed amid crowds; pamphlets surface in the square itself. Halvard's ceremony punctured. Ulyana watches, anonymous among thousands. Beat: climax — history interrupted.

chapters.title: The Fortress Gate
chapters.summary: Public outcry forces a review; prisoners transferred for inquiry. Ulyana waits at the gate as wagons emerge — and her father steps down, aged, unbroken. Beat: catharsis held in restraint.

chapters.title: What Truth Buys
chapters.summary: Aftermath: inquiries opened, but Halvard escapes formal punishment through politics. Bitter victory. Ulyana's POV reckoning with imperfect justice. Beat: the price of survival counted honestly.

chapters.title: Brandt's Quiet Exit
chapters.summary: Brandt resigns, leaving Ulyana a file of records he 'lost' — his own small amendment. Ambiguous grace. Beat: even the compromised can choose once.

chapters.title: Setting the Record
chapters.summary: Ulyana prints the full unexpurgated edition under the shop's own imprint, her father's name restored to the colophon. Beat: authorship reclaimed; belonging found in craft.

chapters.title: The Shop Stays Open
chapters.summary: Months later: the shop thrives, Milo apprenticed properly, Anton departing to testify abroad. Farewell at the loading door where he arrived. Beat: love acknowledged, released.

chapters.title: Compass and Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana's final reflection at the case, setting tomorrow's type: history happens to everyone; the question is who writes it down. She closes the ledger and opens a fresh page. Beat: resolution — visibility chosen, permanently.
